binders: Ω is an arbitrary type equipped with a measurable-space structure.
μ is a measure on Ω equipped with the assumption that it is a probability measure.
X : Ω → ℝ is an arbitrary real-valued function.
K : ℝ is an arbitrary real constant.
hypotheses: X is integrable with respect to μ.
For every λ ∈ ℝ, the function ω ↦ exp(λ X(ω)) is integrable with respect to μ.
For every λ ∈ ℝ, ∫ exp(λ X(ω)) dμ(ω) ≤ exp(K² λ²).
conclusions: The integral (expectation) of X with respect to μ equals 0.
mathematical_definitions: Integrable means almost-everywhere strongly measurable with finite integral norm.
The integral is the real-valued Bochner integral; because μ is a probability measure, it can be read as expectation.
The exponential-moment expression is the moment-generating function value E[exp(λX)].
translation.proposition_plain_english: On a probability space, let X be an integrable real-valued function and K a real number. If for every real λ the function ω ↦ exp(λ X(ω)) is integrable and its integral is at most exp(K² λ²), then the integral of X is zero.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The exponential integrability and bound are required for every real λ, including both positive and negative values.
K is not assumed nonnegative, but only K² occurs, so its sign has no effect.
The conclusion is about the integral of X; the explicit integrability hypothesis ensures this has the intended expectation interpretation.
The assumptions are not intrinsically vacuous: for example, X = 0 satisfies them for every real K.
ambiguities: No material ambiguity remains in the elaborated proposition.
